newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 7.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - July 7.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
FRANKFURT - German media authorities defend their plan to loosen advertising guidelines and dispute that their new recommendations conflict with German advertising law. (Frankfurter Rundschau)
FRANKFURT - The Deutsche Bank has hired multimedia agency Pixel Factory to design the company's Intranet. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Bertelsmann AG, Europe's biggest media conglomerate, says the man who has driven the company's move into multimedia and Internet-related services will become Bertelsmann's chairman next year. The choice of Thomas Middelhoff, the 44-year-old board member in charge of corporate development and multimedia, to replace outgoing chairman Mark Woessner signals a generation change aimed at steering the group into the information age. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Shares in German television network Pro Sieben AG are buoyant and well above their initial public offering price in grey market dealings ahead of the start of share market dealings on Monday. Pro Sieben shares are trading at 106 to 110 marks, according to share market dealers, after earlier trading as high as 112 marks in morning dealings. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Bertelsmann AG posts an operating profit of 1.6 billion marks ($918.4 million) in the year to June 30, chief executive Mark Woessner says. "In 1996/97 we were better than in the year before. I don't know any media company in the world that is doing better," Woessner tells Der Spiegel news magazine. (Reuter)

GUETERSLOH - Bertelsmann AG says it has no plans to buy U.S. publisher McGraw-Hill Inc, denying a report in Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung. But a spokesman declines to comment on a Wall Street Journal report that Bertelsmann will add cash to its partner America Online's bid for rival Compuserve. (Reuter)

BONN - German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt calls for the removal of restrictions on encryption technology, kicking off a two-day conference on Internet commerce attended by 40 government ministers from the European Union, the United States, Russia, Japan and Canada. The issue is expected to be one of the most hotly debated at the conference. (Reuter)

BERLIN - Germany's largest regional public channel, WDR regional channel NDR, Bavaria Film and Studio Hamburg form a new joint venture called German United Distributors Programmvertrieb GmbH, with the aim of internationally marketing television programming rights. (Variety)

BONN - Many Germans seem to believe that not even their beloved summer holiday journeys abroad are sacred from the long reach of Finance Minister Theo Waigel, struggling to plug holes in his budget with new taxes. Thousands of worried viewers flooded the WDR television station with angry calls after the Monitor programme ran a satire claiming Waigel planned a tax of 150 marks on Germans leaving the country on holiday. (Reuter)

BERLIN - German regional television station Puls-TV, in the midst of bankruptcy proceedings, says it is laying off 64 employees and will let the last 60 go at the end of August. Attorney Wolfgang Schroeder, who is overseeing the proceedings, says the channel will continue to be backed until the end of August by newly founded station TV Berlin, owned by Thomas Kirch, son of media mogul Leo Kirch. (Reuter)
LEIPZIG - Channel three of the ARD public broadcasting network boosts its market share in the first half of 1997 to 11.2 percent, ARD says, continuing four years of expansion. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - The upper house of Germany's parliament approves continued transfers of about 5.7 billion marks ($3.3 billion) annually in investment incentives to the formerly communist eastern states and west Berlin until 2004. Starting next year, however, the incentives will take the form of payments rather than the former tax credits, which were harder to audit. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Munich Re is gearing up to fuse its primary insurance units with Victoria Holding AG in a mega-merger that will create an insurance giant to rival market leader Allianz AG. The deal sent Munich Re's shares surging 10 percent. (Reuter)

WALLDORF - Software group SAP AG says that profit growth in the second quarter of 1997 will be similar to the 54-percent rise in pretax profit posted in the first three months of the year. The company also says growth rates in the second half of the year will be slower than the high levels seen in the first half. SAP would give precise first-half results on July 24. (Reuter)

BONN - Retail group Metro AG and its majority shareholder Metro Holding AG say they are in talks with the Dutch retailer SHV Holdings NV about taking over its cash and carry business, the Utrecht-based Makro. "The negotiations are to be concluded as soon as possible," Metro says in a statement. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Daimler-Benz plans to bring a convertible four-seater to the auto market next year, according to the Hamburger Abendblatt. The company refuses to comment. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Women's fashion group Jil Sander AG says at its annual general meeting it expects sales in 1997 to rise almost 10 percent but operating profits to stagnate. The company's sales rose in 1996 to 172.7 million marks from 163.2 million in 1995 but net profit fell to 11.1 million marks in 1996 from 12.4 million a year earlier. (Reuter)

BONN - The consumption of beef in Germany declined by nearly 10 percent in 1996 as Germans turned away from beef and towards fowl, the agriculture ministry says. The per-capita beef consumption in Germany declined by nearly one kg to 10.5 kg, the ministry says, while fowl was up 400 grams to 8.4 kg per capita. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Sportswear company Adidas AG is a leading candidate to join the DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares, statistics published by the Deutsche Boerse show. According to the data, Adidas occupies the 27th position among German companies in terms of market capitalisation and the 29th place in terms of sales. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

FRANKFURT - Christian Koehler moves to Kraft Jacobs Suchard, where he takes over the long-vacant seat of general manager for sweets. Koehler leaves his post of marketing director for Mars unit Effem. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Oliver Biermann is promoted to vice chief executive of Ogilvy & Mather in Duesseldorf. Biefmann was since 1988 a senior advisor for the agency. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Hartmut Liebing is tapped Client Service Director in the Opel unit of Lowe & Partner of Frankfurt. He was previously an account director at MC&LB. (Kress)
